author: Leith Bade <leith@bade.nz>
commit message:
Fix cam2map USEPROJ writing misspelled EquitorialRadius keyword (#6162)

* Fix `cam2map` USEPROJ writing misspelled `EquitorialRadius` keyword

The USEPROJ branch built its Mapping group in C++ and wrote the radius
keyword as EquitorialRadius (missing the 'a') instead of
EquatorialRadius. Beyond the label typo, the later 'copy any defaults
not in the user map from the camera map file' step only checks for
the correctly-spelled name, so it silently added the camera/target's
own default EquatorialRadius alongside the misspelled, unused one --
meaning a user-requested ellipsoid radius from a custom PROJString
was silently overridden by the target's default rather than used.

Adds gtest coverage for the USEPROJ/PROJSTRING code path: asserting
every keyword in the Mapping group it produces, the +type=crs prepend
condition (both when it fires and when it is skipped because the
string already has it), and that an unparseable PROJString or one that
resolves to a valid PROJ object with no associated ellipsoid both throw
rather than silently producing a garbage projection.

Fixes https://github.com/DOI-USGS/ISIS3/issues/6155. Investigated and
fixed with the assistance of Claude Code.

commit message:
Keep the instrument serial number for CSM cubes so jigsaw can read them (#6134)

* Keep the instrument serial number for CSM cubes so jigsaw can read them

jigsaw reads its input cubes into a SerialNumberList, which requires a unique
serial number per cube. A cube that has a CSM sensor model attached (a CsmInfo
group) had its serial number built only from the CSMPlatformID, CSMInstrumentId,
and ReferenceTime fields. That serial number drops the per-image identity, so two
images that share a reference time - as sub-images of a framing instrument do -
receive the same serial number, and jigsaw fails with "Duplicate serial number".

Now the instrument-based serial number is preferred whenever the cube has a
recognized instrument label (which csminit keeps), and the CSM serial number is
used only when there is no usable instrument label. This restores a unique serial
number per image and makes it agree with the serial number the same cube had
before csminit. Fixes DOI-USGS/ISIS3#5482 and DOI-USGS/ISIS3#4240.

Added a test that reproduces the failure: two cubes given the same CsmInfo are
added to a SerialNumberList; it fails with "Duplicate serial number" before this
change and passes after.

This work was done with AI assistance (Claude).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Retrigger CI

Empty commit to re-run the CI. The camera/calibration test failures on the prior
run (VIMS, Dawn VIR, Clipper push-broom, CTX ctxcal) are unrelated to this serial
number change: they fail on the current dev branch without this change on the same
machine, and are floating-point tolerance-edge failures (some use exact double
equality). Re-running to confirm they vary between runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Rethrow when the instrument label has no serial and no CSM fallback

Addresses review feedback on the guarded instrument translation. When
the instrument label cannot be translated and the cube has no CsmInfo
group, there is no source for a serial number, so re-throw the original
error (chained) instead of continuing with an empty mission and
instrument. That would otherwise fail later with a confusing message
about a missing translation file. The CSM fallback is still taken when a
CsmInfo group is present.

Done with AI assistance (Claude).

Address review feedback on the CSM serial number fix.

Remove dead assignments in the mission/instrument catch: mission and

Add a CSM fallback in the instrument-serial branch. A cube with a

commit message:
Fix plot_nonlinear for bivariate smooths in multi-smooth models

Plotting a bivariate smooth from a model with more than one smooth term either errored or silently used the wrong variables:

- `sapply()` returned a list or matrix for `xnames` (depending on the
  mix of smooth dimensions) and only the vector case was handled.
- `fs` and `xnames` were subset by a logical the length of `smooths`
  rather than `labels`, so the first smooth's variables were always
  used regardless of which one was selected.
- `nd` was resampled with indices up to `nrow(xz)` (10000) rather than
  `nrow(nd)`, producing NA rows and a NaN surface whenever the model
  had other covariates.
- The bivariate check was model-wide (`!any(fs)`), so any `bs = "fs"`
  smooth sent bivariate smooths down the univariate path.
